mainTopic: Why רבי יהודה says אין קרבן ציבור חלוק, and how פיגול passes from an offering to its bread but not back
overview: The amud opens with רב פפא's suggestion that רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about an impure part of a קרבן ציבור because they disagree about whether the ציץ is מרצה on things that are eaten. רב הונא בריה דרב נתן, רב אשי and רבינא each knock this down. They point to the בזיכין, which are burned on the מזבח; to the קרבן פסח, where the people are impure; and to the loaves, where רבי יהודה never mentions the ציץ. רבי יוחנן concludes that רבי יהודה had a fixed tradition: אין קרבן ציבור חלוק. A new משנה then teaches that the תודה makes its bread פיגול, and the כבשים of שבועות make their bread פיגול, but never the reverse. The גמרא first tries רב כהנא's idea that the bread is called 'תודה'. It ends up explaining that the bread comes because of the animal (גלל), and shows why the משנה needed both cases. Finally, רבי אלעזר asks רב about a כזית of wrong intent split between the תודה and its bread. רב rules that the bread is פיגול and the תודה is not. The גמרא challenges this with a קל וחומר and begins quoting a ברייתא that questions this kind of קל וחומר, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The argument depends on whether the frontplate helps for eaten items
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים hold that the ציץ brings acceptance for impure items that are eaten. רבי יהודה holds that it does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים think the ציץ brings acceptance for things that are eaten. רבי יהודה thinks the ציץ does not bring acceptance for things that are eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers an explanation for the argument between the חכמים and רבי יהודה. In the case, one part of a communal offering became impure and the other part stayed pure. The explanation is that they disagree about how far the power of the ציץ reaches.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ציץ can make an offering 'accepted' even though something in it became impure. The חכמים say this power also covers items the כהנים eat, so the pure part may still be eaten. רבי יהודה says the ציץ only covers items that go up on the מזבח, so the sprinkling of the blood does not permit the pure part.

keyTerms.meaning: The golden frontplate worn by the כהן גדול
Brings acceptance for an offering, making it count despite impurity
Parts of an offering that are eaten, not burned on the מזבח

steps.confusionAlert: Even according to רבי יהודה, the ציץ does work. The only question is whether it also covers parts that are eaten. Everyone agrees it covers parts that go up on the מזבח.

phrases.aramaic: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל אֲכִילוֹת,
phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: the frontplate brings acceptance for things that are eaten,

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה סָבַר: אֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל אֲכִילוֹת.
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda holds: the frontplate does not bring acceptance for things that are eaten.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבָּנַן סָבְרִי: הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל אֲכִילוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a reason for the argument between רבי יהודה and the חכמים that comes just before this passage.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The argument depends on whether the ציץ is מרצה on אכילות. The חכמים say yes and רבי יהודה says no.

steps.title: They argue even about items burned on the altar
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן challenges רב פפא. The ציץ surely works for items that go up on the מזבח, and they still argue about those.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן said to רב פפא: But what about items that go up on the מזבח? The ציץ brings acceptance for those, and still they argue!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא בריה דרב נתן attacks the explanation from Step 1. He points out that רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue even in a case where the ציץ definitely works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the whole argument were about the ציץ, there should be no argument when the impure item is something burned on the מזבח, because everyone agrees the ציץ covers that. Yet they still argue in such a case. So their argument must come from a different reason.

keyTerms.meaning: Items that go up and are burned on the מזבח
They argue

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב נָתָן לְרַב פָּפָּא:
phrases.english: Rav Huna son of Rav Natan said to Rav Pappa:

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא עוֹלִין, דְּהַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל הָעוֹלִין,
phrases.english: But there are items that go up on the altar, where the frontplate brings acceptance for items that go up,
phrases.notes: He means that even רבי יהודה agrees the ציץ works for these.

phrases.english: and they still argue!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא עוֹלִין, דְּהַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל הָעוֹלִין, וּפְלִיגִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the explanation given in Step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the argument depends on whether the ציץ is מרצה on אכילות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: They also argue about עולין, where everyone agrees the ציץ works. So the ציץ cannot be the reason for the argument.

steps.title: Proof from the two bowls of frankincense
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue when one of the two בזיכין of frankincense becomes impure. רבי יהודה's reason is that אין קרבן ציבור חלוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: If one of the בזיכין became impure, רבי יהודה says both of them are offered in impurity, because a קרבן ציבור is not divided. The חכמים say: the impure one stays in its impurity and the pure one stays in its purity.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to back up the challenge from Step 2. It shows an argument about items burned on the מזבח, where the ציץ is not the issue.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The frankincense in the בזיכין is burned on the מזבח, so the ציץ works for it according to everyone. Even so, רבי יהודה says to treat both bowls as impure, since a communal offering cannot be split into pure and impure parts. The חכמים say each bowl keeps its own status. This shows the true reason behind their argument.

keyTerms.meaning: The two bowls of frankincense placed with the לחם הפנים and later burned on the מזבח
A communal offering brought for all of ישראל
A communal offering is not divided, so it cannot be partly pure and partly impure
Ritual impurity

steps.whyThisMatters: This source shows that רבי יהודה's real reason is the principle that a communal offering is not divided. The power of the ציץ is not his reason.

phrases.english: As it is taught: If one of the bowls of frankincense became impure,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שְׁנֵיהֶם יֵעָשׂוּ בְּטוּמְאָה,
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: both of them are offered in impurity,
because a communal offering is not divided,

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: הַטָּמֵא בְּטוּמְאָתוֹ וְהַטָּהוֹר בְּטׇהֳרָתוֹ.
phrases.english: and the Sages say: the impure one stays in its impurity and the pure one stays in its purity.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for רב הונא's claim in Step 2 that they argue about עולין.
steps.raayaObject: The claim that רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue even about items burned on the מזבח.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא about one impure bowl of frankincense out of the two בזיכין.

steps.title: A second challenge from the impure tribe and the קרבן פסח
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי adds that רבי יהודה applies אין קרבן ציבור חלוק to the קרבן פסח, where one tribe is impure. In that case the ציץ has nothing to do with it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, רב אשי said: Come and hear. רבי יהודה says: Even if one tribe is impure and all the other tribes are pure, they all offer it in impurity, because a communal offering is not divided. And here, what does the frontplate's acceptance have to do with it?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי brings a second challenge to the explanation from Step 1. He uses רבי יהודה's ruling about the קרבן פסח when one tribe is impure.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the people are impure, and the offering itself is not. The ציץ only brings acceptance for impure offerings. It never allows impure people to bring a קרבן. Since רבי יהודה still says everyone brings it in impurity, his reason must be אין קרבן ציבור חלוק, and the ציץ is not part of it.

keyTerms.meaning: And furthermore, which introduces an additional argument
A tribe of ישראל
Ritually pure

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's and רב אשי's challenges both show that רבי יהודה's view comes from the principle that אין קרבן ציבור חלוק. It does not come from a view about whether the ציץ is מרצה on things that are eaten. רבינא adds a third challenge in the next steps.

phrases.aramaic: וְעוֹד, אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע,
phrases.english: And furthermore, Rav Ashi said: Come and hear,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֲפִילּוּ שֵׁבֶט אֶחָד טָמֵא
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: Even if one tribe is impure
phrases.notes: This case is about bringing the קרבן פסח while some of the people are impure.

phrases.english: and all the other tribes are pure, they all offer it in impurity,
because a communal offering is not divided,
phrases.notes: Some versions say 'offerings' in the round brackets; the corrected wording in square brackets says 'offering'. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: and here, what does the frontplate's acceptance have to do with it?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְעוֹד, אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: תָּא שְׁמַע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, separate challenge against the explanation in Step 1, alongside רב הונא's challenge.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רבי יהודה's view depends on the ציץ not being מרצה on אכילות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהודה applies the same principle where the ציץ is completely irrelevant, because the people are impure and the offering is not. So the ציץ cannot be his reason.

steps.title: רבינא brings a משנה about the two loaves and the לחם הפנים
steps.stepSummary: רבינא brings another source. It is a משנה about the שתי הלחם or the לחם הפנים, where only one loaf or one arrangement became impure. רבי יהודה says to burn both, because אין קרבן ציבור חלוק. The חכמים say to burn only the impure one and eat the pure one.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore, didn't רבינא say: Come and hear. If one of the loaves became impure, or one of the arrangements, רבי יהודה says: Both are taken to be burned, because a communal offering is not divided. And the חכמים say: The impure one stays impure, and the pure one may be eaten.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds another argument against רב פפא by quoting a משנה. This step sets up the source; the challenge itself comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This case is about loaves that the כהנים eat, not things burned on the מזבח. That is exactly where רב פפא's ציץ idea should matter most. Yet רבי יהודה's only stated reason is אין קרבן ציבור חלוק.

keyTerms.meaning: Loaves; here, the two loaves (שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם) brought on שָׁבוּעוֹת
Arrangements; the two rows of the לֶחֶם הַפָּנִים (showbread)
The place where disqualified holy items are burned
A communal offering, brought on behalf of all of Israel
Divided; split, so that part is used and part is thrown out

phrases.english: And furthermore, didn't Ravina say:
Come and hear:
If one of the loaves became impure,
phrases.notes: These are the two loaves brought on שבועות.

phrases.english: or one of the arrangements,
phrases.notes: These are the two rows of לחם הפנים. Some versions leave out the round-bracket word, and the square-bracket word is the corrected wording.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says:
Both must go out to the place of burning,
because a communal offering is not divided.
And the Rabbis say:
The impure one stays in its impurity,
and the pure one may be eaten.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a third challenge, after רב הונא's (steps 2–3) and רב אשי's (step 4), against explaining the dispute through the ציץ. It quotes the source that step 6 uses for the attack.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יהודה's reason is אין קרבן ציבור חלוק and not the ציץ
steps.raayaSupportSource: A משנה about one impure loaf of the שתי הלחם or one impure arrangement of the לחם הפנים

steps.title: רבי יהודה should have mentioned the ציץ
steps.stepSummary: If the argument were really about the ציץ, רבי יהודה should have said the loaves are burned because the ציץ does not help for eaten items. He did not say that.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if it is so (that the argument is about the ציץ), he should have said: 'because the ציץ does not bring acceptance for eaten items'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the משנה to attack רב פפא. If the ציץ were the issue, רבי יהודה would have given that reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These loaves are eaten by the כהנים. So the ציץ reason would fit them perfectly. Since רבי יהודה gives a different reason, the ציץ cannot be the real basis of the argument.

keyTerms.meaning: And if it is so; if your explanation were correct
The gold plate on the כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל's forehead, which brings acceptance for some impure offerings
Brings acceptance; makes the offering acceptable
Items that are eaten, as opposed to burned on the מזבח
He should have said

phrases.english: And if it is so,
phrases.notes: He means: if רב פפא were right that the argument is about the ציץ.

phrases.aramaic: לְפִי שֶׁאֵין הַצִּיץ מְרַצֶּה עַל אֲכִילוֹת
phrases.english: 'because the frontplate does not bring acceptance for eaten items'
he should have said!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the challenge out of the משנה quoted in step 5.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב פפא's explanation that רבי יהודה and the חכמים argue about whether the ציץ helps for eaten items
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: In a case of eaten items, רבי יהודה gives the reason אין קרבן ציבור חלוק and never mentions the ציץ. So the ציץ is not his reason.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: a fixed tradition of רבי יהודה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the ציץ explanation. רבי יוחנן says that רבי יהודה had a firm tradition: a communal offering is never split. The whole offering must be treated the same way.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: It is a fixed teaching in the mouth of רבי יהודה that a communal offering is not divided.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives up on רב פפא's idea. It explains רבי יהודה's view as a received tradition: אין קרבן ציבור חלוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא signals that the earlier explanation is rejected. רבי יהודה's ruling does not come from a rule about the ציץ. It comes from a separate tradition about communal offerings: the parts cannot be treated differently. So with the בזיכין and the פסח everything is offered in impurity, and with the loaves both are burned.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; this word drops the earlier approach
A fixed, well-arranged teaching; a firm received tradition
In the mouth of; what this sage held and taught

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה burns the whole communal offering when part of it becomes impure. His reason is not the ציץ. It is his fixed tradition that אין קרבן ציבור חלוק.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yoḥanan said:

phrases.aramaic: תַּלְמוּד עָרוּךְ הוּא בְּפִיו שֶׁל רַבִּי יְהוּדָה,
phrases.english: It is a fixed teaching in the mouth of Rabbi Yehuda,
that a communal offering is not divided.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenges by dropping the ציץ explanation and replacing it.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: רבי יהודה's view comes from a received tradition that אין קרבן ציבור חלוק, not from a rule about the ציץ.

steps.title: New משנה: the תודה can make its loaves פיגול, but not the other way around
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה teaches that a wrong intention about the תודה makes both the animal and its loaves פיגול. A wrong intention about only the loaves makes only the loaves פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The תודה makes the bread פיגול, but the bread does not make the תודה פיגול. How so? If he slaughtered the תודה intending to eat from it tomorrow, both it and the bread are פיגול. If he intended to eat from the bread tomorrow, the bread is פיגול but the תודה is not.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה opens with a new topic: פיגול between an offering and the loaves that come with it. It starts with the תודה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The loaves depend on the animal, so the animal 'pulls' them along. If the intention to eat at the wrong time is about the animal, both become פיגול. The animal does not depend on the loaves, so an intention about the loaves affects only the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Short for מַתְנִיתִין: our משנה
The thanksgiving offering, which comes with loaves of bread
Makes something פִּגּוּל; disqualifies it through an intention to eat it at the wrong time
How so? The משנה is about to show what it means
Tomorrow; after the time allowed for eating

steps.confusionAlert: פיגול here comes from intention, not from anything actually done. Just the thought, at the time of שחיטה, of eating it 'tomorrow' (after its time) is what makes it פיגול.

phrases.english: MISHNA:
The thanks offering makes the bread piggul,
but the bread does not make the thanks offering piggul.
How so? If he slaughtered the thanks offering
intending to eat from it tomorrow,
phrases.notes: The תודה may only be eaten that day and the following night, so 'tomorrow' is too late.

phrases.english: it and the bread are piggul.
If he intended to eat from the bread tomorrow,
the bread is piggul,
and the thanks offering is not piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new משנה with a new topic.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention of פיגול about the תודה makes both the animal and its bread פיגול. An intention about the bread makes only the bread פיגול.

steps.title: The same rule for the כבשים of עצרת and the two loaves
steps.stepSummary: The same rule applies to the lambs brought on שבועות with the שתי הלחם. The lambs can make the loaves פיגול, but the loaves cannot make the lambs פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: The lambs make the bread פיגול, but the bread does not make the lambs פיגול. How so? If one slaughters the lambs intending to eat from them tomorrow, both they and the bread are פיגול. If he intended to eat the bread tomorrow, the bread is פיגול but the lambs are not.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה repeats the same pattern for a second case: the two כבשים of שבועות and their two loaves.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is the communal version of the תודה case. Here too the loaves depend on the animals, but the animals do not depend on the loaves. So פיגול moves in only one direction: from the animals to the loaves.

keyTerms.meaning: Lambs; here, the two lambs brought on שָׁבוּעוֹת together with the שְׁתֵּי הַלֶּחֶם
Made פִּגּוּל; disqualified because of a wrong-time intention

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול moves from the animal offering to its loaves, never from the loaves to the animal. This is true both for the תודה and for the כבשים of שבועות.

phrases.english: The lambs make the bread piggul,
phrases.notes: These are the two lambs brought on שבועות together with the two loaves.

phrases.english: but the bread does not make the lambs piggul.
How so? One who slaughters the lambs
intending to eat from them tomorrow,
they and the bread are piggul.
If he intended to eat the bread tomorrow,
the bread is piggul,
and the lambs are not piggul.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the rule of step 8 to a second, parallel case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: An intention of פיגול about the lambs of שבועות makes both the lambs and the loaves פיגול. An intention about the loaves makes only the loaves פיגול.

steps.title: What is the reason for the one-way rule?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why a wrong intention about the תודה makes the loaves פיגול too.
steps.simpleTranslation: GEMARA: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens its discussion of the משנה by asking for the reason behind its rule. This sets up the next move, where a possible answer is offered.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said that פיגול passes from the תודה to the loaves but not from the loaves to the תודה. The גמרא wants to know what makes the connection work in only one direction.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
An offering made unfit by a wrong intention about when it will be eaten or offered

phrases.english: GEMARA: What is the reason?
phrases.notes: He is asking why a wrong intention about the תודה makes its loaves פיגול as well.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the משנה quoted in steps 8 and 9.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source or logic for why the תודה makes the loaves פיגול but not the reverse.

steps.title: Suggestion: the loaves are called 'תודה'
steps.stepSummary: Maybe the reason is רב כהנא's teaching that the loaves of the תודה are themselves called 'תודה'.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it is because of רב כהנא's teaching: רב כהנא said, from where do we know that the loaves of the תודה are called 'תודה'? From the פסוק, 'He shall offer with the thanks-offering sacrifice loaves.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries out a first answer. It suggests that the loaves count as part of the תודה, because the תורה calls them by that name.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the loaves are called 'תודה', then a wrong intention about the תודה also covers the loaves. The word אילימא tells us this answer is only a trial, and it will be tested next.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggested answer that will be tested)
The loaves brought with a thanks offering
From where do we know?

phrases.english: If you say it is because of Rav Kahana's teaching,
for Rav Kahana said:
From where do we know that the loaves of a thanks offering
are called 'thanks offering'?
As it says: 'He shall offer with the sacrifice of thanks offering, loaves.'
phrases.notes: ויקרא ז:יב. The words 'תודה' and 'loaves' sit right next to each other.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first possible answer to the question in step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The loaves are called 'תודה', so a wrong intention about the תודה covers them too.

steps.title: Then it should work in reverse too
steps.stepSummary: If the loaves and the תודה share a name, the loaves should also make the תודה פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the reverse should also be true.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the suggestion. If the loaves count as 'תודה', why shouldn't פיגול pass from the loaves to the animal too?
steps.deeperAnalysis: A shared name seems to tie the two things together equally. But the משנה says the loaves do not make the תודה פיגול, so the suggestion looks like it does not fit.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
The reverse

phrases.english: If so, the reverse should also be true,

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the רב כהנא answer from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The suggestion that the shared name 'תודה' is the reason.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A shared name should link the two both ways, but the משנה says the link goes only one way.

steps.title: The name goes only one way
steps.stepSummary: The bread is called 'תודה', but the תודה is never called 'bread'.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is not difficult. The bread is called 'תודה', but the תודה is not called 'bread'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the רב כהנא answer. The name is one-directional, so the rule is one-directional too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק calls the loaves by the name of the animal, but nowhere calls the animal by the name of the loaves. So a wrong intention about the animal covers the loaves, but not the other way around.

keyTerms.meaning: This is not difficult
Is called

phrases.english: This is not difficult:
the bread is called 'thanks offering,'
but the thanks offering is not called 'bread.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 12.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Shows the name link is one-directional.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A shared name links both items equally.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only the bread carries the name of the תודה, so the rule works only from the תודה to the bread.

steps.title: The lambs case breaks this explanation
steps.stepSummary: In the case of the lambs of עצרת, the bread is never called 'lambs', so the name idea cannot explain that case.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what the משנה teaches: the lambs make the bread פיגול, and the bread does not make the lambs פיגול. Where do we find that bread is called 'lambs'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a stronger challenge against the רב כהנא answer. The same one-way rule applies to the lambs, but there is no פסוק that calls the bread 'lambs'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The name idea might work for the תודה, but the משנה gives the same rule for the כבשים and the שתי הלחם. Since no shared name exists there, the name cannot be the real reason behind the rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The two lambs brought on שבועות with the שתי הלחם
Make something פיגול
Where do we find?

phrases.english: But what about that which is taught:
the lambs make the bread piggul,
and the bread does not make the lambs piggul,
where do we find that bread
is called 'lambs'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Renews the attack on the רב כהנא answer, now using the lambs case from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The name-based explanation from steps 11 and 13.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same rule applies to the lambs, where there is no shared name, so the name cannot be the reason.

steps.title: The real reason: the bread comes because of the offering
steps.stepSummary: The bread is brought because of the main offering, not the other way around, so פיגול flows only from the main offering to the bread.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, isn't this the reason: the bread comes because of the תודה, and the תודה does not come because of the bread. The bread comes because of the lambs, and the lambs do not come because of the bread.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops the רב כהנא answer and gives the true reason. The animal is the main part, and the bread is only an add-on to it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the bread exists only because of the animal, a problem in the animal spreads to the bread. The animal does not depend on the bread, so a problem in the bread stays in the bread. This one idea explains both the תודה and the lambs.

keyTerms.meaning: On account of, because of
Rather, isn't it (introduces the real explanation)

steps.whatToRemember: פיגול spreads from the main offering to the bread that comes because of it (גלל), but never from the bread back to the main offering.
steps.confusionAlert: The reason is not that the bread is called 'תודה'. That idea was dropped. The reason is that the bread depends on the animal.
steps.whyThisMatters: This single principle covers both cases in the משנה, while the name idea could cover only the תודה.

phrases.english: Rather, isn't this the reason:
the bread comes because of the thanks offering,
and the thanks offering does not come because of the bread;
phrases.notes: Some versions have the words in round brackets; the words in square brackets are the corrected wording. The meaning is the same.

phrases.english: the bread comes because of the lambs,
and the lambs do not come because of the bread.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After step 14 knocks out the name idea, this gives the true answer to step 10.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The bread is secondary to the animal (גלל), so פיגול passes from the animal to the bread only.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The one-way rule rests on which item depends on which.

steps.title: Why the משנה needed both cases
steps.stepSummary: The lambs case was needed, because lambs and bread are waved together, and we might have thought פיגול would then spread both ways.
steps.simpleTranslation: Both cases are needed. If the משנה had taught only the תודה, I would say the bread does not make the תודה פיגול only because they are not waved together. But the lambs are waved together with the bread, so I might say a wrong intention about the bread makes the lambs פיגול too. So the lambs case is needed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the משנה teaches the same rule twice. Each case adds something we would not have known from the other.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תודה and its loaves are not waved together, so their link is weak. The lambs and the שתי הלחם are waved together, which might make their link strong enough to work both ways. The משנה teaches that even so, the bread does not make the lambs פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Both are needed (each teaching adds something new)
Waving of an offering in the בית המקדש
Are tied to each other
It taught us

steps.whatToRemember: Even when the bread and the lambs are waved together, the bread still cannot make the lambs פיגול.

phrases.english: And both are needed,
for if it had taught us only the thanks offering,
I would say it is only there that when one makes the bread piggul,
the thanks offering does not become piggul,

phrases.aramaic: מִשּׁוּם דְּלָא הוּזְקְקוּ זֶה לָזֶה בִּתְנוּפָה,
phrases.english: because they are not tied to each other in the waving,
but the lambs,
which are tied to the bread in the waving,
I might say that when one makes the bread piggul,
the lambs should become piggul too;
so it is needed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After finding one reason for both cases, explains why the משנה still needed to state both.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The lambs case teaches that even waving together does not let the bread make the lambs פיגול.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר's question about half-and-half intent
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר asks רב: if a כהן slaughters a תודה planning to eat a כזית from the animal and its bread together tomorrow, what happens with פיגול?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר asked רב: If someone slaughters the thanks offering intending to eat an olive-bulk from it and from its bread tomorrow, what is the law about פיגול?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר asks רב a new question. The כהן's wrong plan covers one כזית made up of part animal and part bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Until now we had a full כזית planned from one item. Here the כזית is split between the animal and the bread, so neither alone has a full measure. The question is whether the two halves add up.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering made invalid because the כהן planned to eat it after its proper time
An olive-sized amount, the minimum measure for פיגול
The thanks offering, which is brought together with loaves of bread
Tomorrow, after the allowed eating time

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar asked Rav:
One who slaughters the thanks offering
intending to eat an olive-bulk from it and from its bread tomorrow,
phrases.notes: He means one כזית in total, part from the animal and part from the bread.

phrases.english: what is the law about becoming פיגול?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question built on the rule that פיגול flows from the animal to the bread but not the other way.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether a כזית of wrong intent split between the animal and its bread creates פיגול.

steps.title: Narrowing the question to the bread
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that the animal is obviously not פיגול. His real question is whether the animal's half joins the bread's half to make the bread פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: I have no question about the thanks offering itself. If even a full olive-bulk from the bread does not make it פיגול, then half from it and half from the bread surely won't. My question is about the bread: does the thanks offering's half combine with the bread's half to make the bread פיגול, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר sharpens his question. He sets aside the animal and asks only about the bread.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We already learned that intent about the bread never makes the animal פיגול, even with a full כזית, so a half from the bread cannot do it. But the bread can become פיגול from the animal's intent. So the open question is whether the half about the animal combines with the half about the bread to make the bread פיגול.

keyTerms.meaning: Combines, joins together to make a full measure
I have no question about it
Now, if even... (used to argue that something is obvious)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think he is asking about the animal. He says clearly that the animal is not פיגול. His question is only about the bread.

phrases.english: About the thanks offering I have no question,
now, if the whole olive-bulk is from its bread, it does not become פיגול,
so with part from it and part from its bread, is there any question?

phrases.aramaic: כִּי קָא מִיבַּעְיָא לִי לְאִיפַּגּוֹלֵי לֶחֶם,
phrases.english: When I ask, it is about the bread becoming פיגול:
does the thanks offering combine
to make the bread פיגול, or not?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Refines the question of step 17 to focus only on the bread.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether intent about the animal combines with intent about the bread to make the bread פיגול.

steps.title: רב answers that the bread is פיגול
steps.stepSummary: רב answers that in this case too the bread is פיגול and the תודה is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Even in this case, the bread is פיגול and the thanks offering is not.
steps.whatsHappening: רב answers רבי אלעזר. The two halves combine to make the bread פיגול, but the animal stays fine.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since פיגול flows from the animal to the bread, the animal's half can count toward the bread. Together with the bread's half, there is a full כזית, so the bread is פיגול. The animal is not, because the bread's half can't count toward it.

keyTerms.meaning: Even in this case
Made פיגול, invalid

phrases.english: He said to him: Even in this case,
the bread is פיגול
and the thanks offering is not פיגול.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 18.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The halves combine for the bread: the bread is פיגול, the תודה is not.

steps.title: A קל וחומר says the bread should not be פיגול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב with a קל וחומר: the animal, which causes the פיגול, is not פיגול, so surely the bread, which tried and failed to cause פיגול, should not be פיגול.
steps.simpleTranslation: But why? Let us say a קל וחומר: If the thanks offering, which makes the bread פיגול, is not itself made פיגול, then the bread, which came to make the offering פיגול but did not, surely should not become פיגול!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא questions רב's ruling using a קל וחומר. It argues the bread should come out not פיגול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In this case the animal's half helps make the bread פיגול, yet the animal is not פיגול. The bread's half tried to make the animal פיגול and failed. The argument: if the one that succeeds stays clean, the one that failed should surely stay clean too.

keyTerms.meaning: An argument from a lighter case to a stronger case
But why?
Is it not logical?

steps.confusionAlert: Keep track of who is who: "the one that makes פיגול" is the animal; "the one that came to make פיגול but did not" is the bread.

phrases.english: But why? Let us say a קל וחומר:
If the thanks offering, which makes it פיגול,
phrases.notes: "It" is the bread. The animal's half helps make the bread פיגול.

phrases.english: is not itself made פיגול,
then the one that came to make it פיגול and did not,
phrases.notes: This is the bread, whose half could not make the animal פיגול.

phrases.english: is it not logical that it should not become פיגול?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב's answer in step 19.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's ruling that the bread is פיגול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: קל וחומר: if the animal, which causes פיגול, is not פיגול, the bread, which failed to cause פיגול, should surely not be פיגול.

steps.title: Questioning whether this kind of קל וחומר works
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether such a קל וחומר is valid at all, and starts quoting a ברייתא about an incident to show it is not.
steps.simpleTranslation: But do we say a קל וחומר like this? Wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: There was an incident with one...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the קל וחומר from the last step. It is setting up a ברייתא, which continues in the next part, to show this kind of reasoning is not used.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of defending רב directly, the גמרא attacks the method of the challenge. If this style of קל וחומר is not accepted, the question against רב falls away. The proof is a story in a ברייתא that begins here.

keyTerms.meaning: In this way, like this
An incident, a story that actually happened

phrases.aramaic: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא?
phrases.english: But do we say a קל וחומר like this?
But was it not taught: There was an incident with one...

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמִי אָמְרִינַן קַל וָחוֹמֶר כִּי הַאי גַוְונָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the method of the קל וחומר in step 20, quoting a ברייתא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The validity of the קל וחומר used against רב.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: This style of קל וחומר may not be accepted, as a ברייתא about an incident will show.
